input.quote: Upon reasonable request not more than once during any calendar year, and with reasonable notice, the Servicer will give the Issuer, the Depositor, the Parent Support Provider, the Administrator, the Owner Trustee and the Indenture Trustee (or their representatives) access to the records and documents to conduct a review of the Servicer's performance under this Agreement.
input.rationale: The direction of the audit/inspection rights in this agreement is inverted relative to the rule: every review right runs against the counterparty, not against us. Section 3.6 (p0131) gives the Issuer, Depositor and other transaction parties an annual, reasonable-notice review of the Servicer's (Cellco's) records at Cellco's offices, and Section 3.9(e) (p0146) gives the Depositor, Issuer and Indenture Trustee access to the Receivable Files and receivables systems held by Cellco as Custodian; the Regulation AB items (Compliance Statement, Servicing Assessment, Attestation Report and Annual Certification) are likewise deliverables of Cellco, at its cost. No provision grants Cellco or any other party an audit, inspection or verification right against the Issuer or the Depositor, and there is no obligation for us to bear audit costs or to grant access to our systems. Accordingly the rule's concerns (frequency, notice, cost, system access binding the customer) are not engaged, and these clauses benefit our party, so we do not redline them. Noted only for the record: the review right we hold is exercisable at the Servicer's offices and is subject to Cellco's security, confidentiality, privacy and data protection policies, which is customary for this deal type.
